rows.old: No token found, please login again
rows.new: Couldn't send your question. Your sign-in has expired. Your question isn't saved. Copy it, then reload the page to sign in again.
rows.why: "Token" is an implementation word; the cause is a sign-in that has ended, and the way out is a reload. "Session" is kept for analytics (§ Terminology). This is the `expired` cause, not the retryable one: `§ Voice and tone › Errors` supersedes the Phase 4 hand-off, which put "No token" under retryable. There is no Retry, because trying again with no sign-in cannot work. What the student sees, from the code: the question leaves the composer when the send starts and stays in the thread (`ChatCore.tsx:1041`); the no-token branch then shows this toast and returns before anything is sent (`ChatCore.tsx:762-768`), so the question is never saved, and the conversation a reload restores is read back from the server (`ChatCore.tsx:253-269`) without it. A reload reaches the sign-in page, because every path that drops the token drops the stored user too (`middleware.ts:27-28`, `:47`, `:66-67`, `:82-83`) and the route guard sends a user-less visit to it (`ProtectedRoute.tsx:51`). No control is added: that would be a flow change. The compare lane draws the same sentence in its bubble (`useChatLane.ts:124-127`). No "still in the form" sentence: the question leaves the box when the send starts (ChatCore.tsx:1041) and the no-token branch returns before anything is sent or saved (ChatCore.tsx:762-768), so there is no form to keep. (C9: Yifrah; Nielsen #9)

rows.why: The wait for the first step or token had no words: `Loader.tsx:15` draws the cycling dots and nothing else, for a tutor message's `typing` (`ChatMessages.tsx:377` and `:452`), against the brief's "never the only signal" (G9, `§ Companion` principle 4). It now draws the word first and the text dots after it, as the Phase 3 loading row has it ("Thinking…" + dots): the dots are the word's ellipsis, built up one, two, three and resting as "…" when motion is reduced (`§ Components`, the Loading rule, Phase 3), so it reads "Thinking…" at rest. "Thinking…" is the user's own wording and the one concession to `§ Voice`'s candour: it names the wait before the first step; once a step runs its label names the step (`§ Step labels`), and a step with no name reads "Working…" (SR-6.49). {dots} is the cycling ".", "..", "..." the loader draws every 500 ms, unchanged: real text from the component's own interval (`Loader.tsx:5-13`), not a CSS pseudo-element, in its own element and decorative (`aria-hidden`), so `Loader.test.tsx`'s dot queries stay valid and a screen reader reads the word once; a CSS-drawn replacement would change those six tests. (C13: Nielsen #1; Doherty threshold)

rows.old: You have been granted access to Kiwi as per your request. You can now log in from the website.
rows.new: You can now sign in to Kiwi with the email address this message was sent to.
rows.why: "As per your request" is a claim the product cannot back; the sentence says what changed and how to use it. It makes no claim about when the account is created. An earlier draft added "If you haven't signed in before, Kiwi sets up your account the first time you do", which is false for a recipient whose account an administrator created with a password: the System email page sends this template to any user the administrator selects (`email.controller.ts:392-421`, `email.service.ts:254`), and an administrator-created password account exists from the moment the administrator submits the form (`auth.controller.ts:51-60` and `auth.service.ts:145-186`: `registerUser` creates the user, its allowlist entry and its enrollments at once). The first sentence holds for every recipient: a pending user signs in with Google, a password account with its password. (C6: Podmajersky terminology agreement; Nielsen #4)

rows.new: You've been added to {className}{ ({professorName})} on Kiwi.
rows.why: A contraction in the same quiet voice. The parenthesis after the class name is kept: the source writes it only when the instructor's name is set (`professorName ? ... : ''`, `email.templates.ts:96` and `:120`), so the part in the second braces is left out when the name is not set, and the spec's email table quotes this exact string. The dialog's prefilled message uses the sentence without that part (A-16.43): the dialog does not know the name. (C8: Podmajersky; Yifrah: we-language)
